title: 1 May and BMS: how the movement marks the day
author: Editorial Desk
summary: BMS observes 1 May as a working day for social service and keeps 17 September as its labour festival.
body:
1 May is observed in many countries as International Workers' Day. India's first May Day was held in Madras in 1923.

## The BMS approach

BMS does not hold May Day as its own festival, preferring **Vishwakarma Jayanti** on 17 September. Even so, its units frequently use 1 May for **service**: blood donation, health camps, felicitation of senior workers and meetings on current issues.

## The argument behind it

The BMS website explains that May Day arises from the class-conflict tradition, while Vishwakarma Jayanti reflects the Indian view of labour as a creative and sacred act. This was discussed in an earlier post.

## What both days share

- Recognition of the **eight-hour day**, which the workers' struggle brought about.
- Attention to **safety and dignity** at work.
- A reminder that **organised effort** gets results.

## Questions for the day

On any day that honours labour, it is worth asking whether the workers around you have a written contract, a wage slip and a day off.
